control: Хранить events: composition, serial issue, first edition, revision, translation, collection, digitization.
needed_sources: GHP/CWMG metadata; BAWS; bibliographies; manuscript catalogues.
problem: Датировка: идея ≠ первая печать ≠ collected edition
risk: Поздняя публикация или редакция может быть принята за дату мысли; serial text — за finished book.

control: Model distributed authorship and clause genealogy; preserve Ambedkar’s distinctive interventions without monopoly claim.
needed_sources: Draft Constitution; CAD; Parliament; constitutional histories.
risk: Heroic shorthand erases B. N. Rau, committees, S. N. Mukherjee, Assembly and amendment process.

control: Build temporal position nodes linked to exact journal issue/text and audience.
needed_sources: CWMG/GHP; Harijan/Young India; Annihilation editions; caste scholarship.
risk: Single quotations from different decades create false consistency or easy acquittal/condemnation.

control: Store Communal Award, statements, negotiation sequence, signatories, seat formula and later evaluations separately.
needed_sources: Pact text; Round Table records; Biswas; electoral history.
problem: Poona Pact: consent, coercion and representation
risk: Signed agreement can conceal fast, political pressure and disagreement about constituency design.

control: Use reciprocal polemicizes_with and contested_by edges; quote positions in time and genre.
needed_sources: Annihilation + Gandhi reply; nationalist counter-history; Radical Equality.
problem: False reconciliation of Gandhi and Ambedkar
risk: Commemorative narratives turn polemic into complementary division of labour.

control: Make institutions and media first-class nodes; figure nodes cannot own the whole graph.
needed_sources: Journal runs; organizational records; committee reports; editorial histories.
risk: Ideas detach from presses, movements, oppressed publics, committees and editors.

control: Store category, authority, date, jurisdiction and self-description; map community agency and state classification.
needed_sources: Census/law/commission records; Ambedkar memoranda; caste histories.
risk: Depressed Classes, minority, caste and Scheduled Castes may be treated as timeless natural groups.

control: Preserve original term in quotations/metadata; add normalized search labels and caution notes.
needed_sources: Periodicals; BAWS; Dalit studies; lexicographic histories.
risk: Anachronistic substitution hides power, contest and changing self-naming.

control: Create work–expression–manifestation nodes; record translator, script, publication venue and version relation.
needed_sources: GHP editions; vernacular bibliographies; BAWS translations; press archives.
risk: English editions look primary while Gujarati/Marathi conceptual choices vanish.

control: Treat as modern philosophical-hermeneutic reconstruction; map canonical sources and deliberate transformations.
needed_sources: Buddha and His Dhamma editions; Buddhist studies; Ambedkar scholarship.
risk: Either dismissed as politics, or projected backward as unchanged ancient doctrine.

control: Use incoming/outgoing corrections; include Hindu Code Bill and gendered institutions in internal queue.
needed_sources: Rege; Omvedt; legal histories; women’s movement archives.
risk: Two-man framing obscures Savitribai Phule, women in anti-caste movements, family law and Dalit feminist critique.

control: Record platform, coverage, OCR, rights, update date, missing ranges and physical archive references.
needed_sources: Official portal documentation; library catalogues; digitization audits.
risk: CWMG/BAWS and polished constitutional sites may overshadow missing newspapers, drafts and vernacular copies.

contribution: ID, launch order, master dates, A/5, исходные seeds, медиумы, handoff и master-risk.
reliability: Канонична для архитектуры ToS; внешняя историческая проверка обязательна.
source_label: [M0] Таблица III ToS v1.0 · T3-40

contribution: Swaraj, critique of modern civilization, parliament, professions, machinery, means/ends; edition sequence 1909–1910.
reliability: Очень высокая для текста/факсимиле; сравнивать Gujarati, authorial English и поздние editions.
source_label: [P01] Hind Swaraj / Indian Home Rule
source_type: Первичный трактат; Gujarati serial + English expression

contribution: Практическая генеалогия satyagraha, organization, discipline, suffering and negotiation.
reliability: Высокая; retrospective narration must be checked against contemporaneous Indian Opinion.
source_label: [P02] Satyagraha in South Africa

contribution: Связывает nonviolence с communal unity, khadi, village industries, sanitation, women, anti-untouchability and basic education.
reliability: Очень высокая; хранить 1941, revised 1945 и позднейшие print manifestations отдельно.
source_label: [P03] Constructive Programme: Its Meaning and Place

contribution: Issue-level circulation, translation, public correction and movement timing; portal also lists Young India, Navajivan, Harijan and related journals.
reliability: Очень высокая как факсимильный вход; completeness/OCR and language balance require audit.
source_label: [P04] Indian Opinion and Gandhi journal corpus

contribution: Changing positions across Young India/Harijan, speeches, letters and the reply appended to Annihilation of Caste.
reliability: Высокая only at text/date level; опасно цитировать как timeless single doctrine.
source_access: CWMG + Gandhi journal archive + Columbia MSE appendix
source_label: [P05] Gandhi caste/varṇa/untouchability writings and 1936 reply

contribution: Paper delivered 9 May 1916; first printed in Indian Antiquary, May 1917; early mechanism account centred on endogamy and enclosure.
reliability: Очень высокая for normalized text and bibliographic layer; consult original journal facsimile for material witness.
source_label: [P06] Castes in India: Their Mechanism, Genesis and Development

contribution: Systematic critique of caste, graded inequality, social reform, authority of śāstra and political prerequisites; 1937 edition adds Gandhi exchange.
reliability: Очень высокая; record first/second/third editions and translation genealogy separately.
source_label: [P07] Annihilation of Caste
source_type: Undelivered address / self-published tract / expanded polemic

contribution: Ambedkar’s 1945 analysis of nationalist representation, Congress claims and Depressed Classes politics.
reliability: Очень высокая for collected text; verify first and revised editions.
source_label: [P08] What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables

contribution: Fundamental rights, minority safeguards, representation and state-economic design; submitted in 1947.
reliability: Очень высокая; do not read as identical with final Constitution.
source_label: [P09] States and Minorities

contribution: Six cases of untouchability as evidentiary method; manuscript c. 1935–1936, first published as a booklet in 1990.
reliability: Очень высокая for survival history; bracketed section labels are editorial.
source_label: [P10] Waiting for a Visa

contribution: Ambedkar’s modern reconstruction of Buddha, Dhamma, morality, social equality and reason; manuscript completed/revised in 1956, first edition 1957.
reliability: Высокая; posthumous editorial and manuscript questions must remain visible.
source_label: [P11] The Buddha and His Dhamma

contribution: Conversion as philosophical-institutional act; equality, refusal of Brahmanical authority, community and Dhamma.
reliability: Высокая where transcript/provenance is known; later standardized vow lists require version control.
source_label: [P12] Nagpur conversion speeches, vows and late Buddhist corpus

contribution: Separate electorates versus joint electorates with reserved seats; fast, pressure, consent and representation; pact dated 24 September 1932.
reliability: Очень высокая for edited pact text and contextual dossier; consult official/archival witnesses for documentary genealogy.
source_label: [P13] Communal Award–Poona Pact dossier

contribution: Submitted 21 February 1948 after scrutiny of B. N. Rau’s draft; 315 articles, public circulation, amendments and Assembly introduction.
reliability: Очень высокая; explicitly demonstrates distributed authorship and version sequence.
source_label: [P14] Draft Constitution of India 1948

contribution: Ambedkar introduces the Draft, defends institutional choices and addresses objections about federalism, villages and constitutional design.
reliability: Очень высокая; edited paragraph numbering should be cross-checked against official scan when quoting.
source_label: [P15] Constituent Assembly Debates · 4 November 1948

contribution: Social democracy; liberty–equality–fraternity; graded inequality; constitutional methods and dangers to democracy.
reliability: Очень высокая; preserve debate context and speaker sequence.
source_label: [P16] Constituent Assembly Debates · 25 November 1949

contribution: Final constitutional architecture, preamble, rights, remedies, institutions and later amendment history.
reliability: Authoritative current legal text; for T3-40 distinguish original 1950 text from later amendments.
source_label: [P17] Constitution of India 1950 / official constitutional text

contribution: Books, journals, CWMG, chronology, images and archival metadata; facsimile-first access.
reliability: Очень высокая discovery layer; portal metadata and interfaces sometimes require manual validation.
source_access: Sabarmati Ashram Preservation and Memorial Trust
source_label: [D01] Gandhi Heritage Portal

contribution: One-hundred-volume English series and supplementary/editorial documentation; source chronology and full-text retrieval.
reliability: Very high, but not neutral: collected-edition selection, translation and dating must be modelled.
source_label: [D02] The Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi · CWMG

contribution: Indian Opinion, Navajivan, Young India, Harijan, Harijan Bandhu, Harijan Sevak and related serials.
reliability: Очень высокая for facsimile access; audit missing pages/issues and OCR.
source_label: [D03] Gandhi journals interface

contribution: English and Hindi volumes, downloadable PDFs and stable entry into major Ambedkar works.
reliability: Очень высокая as official collected corpus; first editions, manuscript states and editorial notes remain distinct.
source_access: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
source_label: [D04] Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches · BAWS

contribution: Searchable text, annotations, appendices, timeline and connected primary texts.
reliability: Очень высокая; pedagogical annotations are secondary layers, not Ambedkar’s own text.
source_label: [D05] Columbia Ambedkar / Annihilation of Caste MSE

contribution: Normalized texts, bibliographic notes, chronology and links to difficult-to-find writings.
reliability: Высокая; not a complete critical edition and occasionally relies on older biographies.
source_label: [D06] Columbia/Pritchett Ambedkar text and chronology hub

contribution: Historical constitutions, petitions, committee reports, drafts, 167 plenary debate days, members and thematic search.
reliability: Очень высокая for navigation and paragraph-level citation; maintain link to official scans.
source_label: [D07] ConstitutionofIndia.net database

contribution: Assembly composition, sessions, committees, procedural history and digitized debates.
reliability: Authoritative institutional layer; interface metadata should be captured.
source_label: [D08] Parliament of India · Constituent Assembly

contribution: Hindi/English scans and official historical debate witnesses.
reliability: Очень высокая material witness; OCR/searchability varies.
source_label: [D09] Sansad e-Library · Constituent Assembly Draft Making Debates

contribution: Current and language editions, amendment-aware official text and publication metadata.
reliability: Authoritative for present law; not a substitute for the 1949–1950 historical text-state.
source_label: [D10] Legislative Department / India Code constitutional editions

contribution: Понятия colonialism, empire, domination, anti-colonial critique; situates Gandhi and wider political theory.
limitations: Широкая рамка; не заменяет South Asian primary corpus.
source_label: [S01] “Colonialism” · Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

contribution: Аргумент о глубокой связи Gandhi’s political strategies with epistemological and ethical commitments.
limitations: Сильная philosophical reconstruction; требует проверки против caste and institutional histories.
source_label: [S02] Akeel Bilgrami, “Gandhi, the Philosopher” (2003)

contribution: Nonviolence as realist politics, social interdependence and restraint rather than moral idealism alone.
limitations: Фокус на Gandhian politics; limited for Ambedkar/caste comparison.
source_label: [S03] Karuna Mantena, “Another Realism: The Politics of Gandhian Nonviolence”

contribution: Reliable text, contextual introductions, glossary and edition history of Hind Swaraj.
limitations: English-centered; use Gujarati witnesses and journal context alongside.
source_label: [S04] Anthony J. Parel (ed.), Gandhi: Hind Swaraj and Other Writings

contribution: Coherent account of human nature, modernity, state, nonviolence, community and pluralism.
limitations: Systematization can smooth chronology and internal inconsistency.
source_label: [S05] Bhikhu Parekh, Gandhi’s Political Philosophy

contribution: Multiple fields: religion, politics, economics, nonviolence, reception and critique.
limitations: Companion format; chapters differ in method and evidence.
source_label: [S06] Judith M. Brown & Anthony Parel (eds.), The Cambridge Companion to Gandhi

contribution: Equality, faith, finitude, nonviolence and resistance; resists secular/religious simplification.
limitations: Conceptually dense; must be triangulated with journal chronology and caste critique.
source_label: [S07] Ajay Skaria, Unconditional Equality: Gandhi’s Religion of Resistance

contribution: Violence/nonviolence, sacrifice, politics and global conceptual setting.
limitations: Interpretive intervention, not a comprehensive corpus history.
source_label: [S08] Faisal Devji, The Impossible Indian: Gandhi and the Temptation of Violence

contribution: Sustained reading of irreducible tension between Gandhi and Ambedkar around equality, sovereignty and democracy.
limitations: Deliberately philosophical; needs institutional and social-history complements.
source_label: [S09] Aishwary Kumar, Radical Equality: Ambedkar, Gandhi, and the Risk of Democracy

contribution: Ambedkar–Gandhi encounter, Dalit politics, cultural memory and non-reconciliatory comparison.
limitations: Essay form and posthumous editorial arrangement require chapter-level use.
source_label: [S10] D. R. Nagaraj, The Flaming Feet and Other Essays

contribution: Thematic access to caste, democracy, representation, religion, economy and constitution with scholarly framing.
limitations: Selection is not a substitute for BAWS and original editions.
source_label: [S11] Valerian Rodrigues (ed.), The Essential Writings of B. R. Ambedkar

contribution: Ambedkar, Dewey, rhetoric, Buddhism and pragmatist transformation; strengthens epistemology/method layer.
limitations: Do not reduce Ambedkar to Dewey reception; local anti-caste genealogy remains autonomous.
source_label: [S12] Scott R. Stroud, The Evolution of Pragmatism in India

contribution: Movements, representation, political strategy, institutions and long afterlife.
limitations: Political biography frame can underplay textual versioning and philosophy of religion.
source_label: [S13] Christophe Jaffrelot, Dr Ambedkar and Untouchability

contribution: Caste, embodiment, violence, representation, law and modern political subjectivity.
limitations: Theoretical emphasis; use primary organizational archives for local detail.
source_label: [S14] Anupama Rao, The Caste Question: Dalits and the Politics of Modern India

contribution: Mahar movement, Ambedkarite organization, terminology, conversion and Dalit public formation.
limitations: Some essays reflect earlier historiographic stages; update with recent Dalit studies.
source_label: [S15] Eleanor Zelliot, From Untouchable to Dalit

contribution: Non-Brahman and Dalit movements, Phule–Ambedkar genealogy, colonial structure and democratic struggle.
limitations: Broad movement synthesis; direct influence claims need text-level confirmation.
source_label: [S16] Gail Omvedt, Dalits and the Democratic Revolution

contribution: Gendered caste, Ambedkar’s critique of Hindu social order and feminist reclamation.
limitations: Normative intervention; indispensable corrective to male-dyad framing.
source_label: [S17] Sharmila Rege, Against the Madness of Manu

contribution: Classic account of Assembly, committees, social revolution and constitutional design.
limitations: Foundational but older; update distributed authorship and archival interpretation.
source_label: [S18] Granville Austin, The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation

contribution: Electoral rolls, universal franchise, bureaucracy and democratic institution-building beyond elite constitution-making.
limitations: Post-1947 administrative emphasis; not a full philosophy of the Constitution.
source_label: [S19] Ornit Shani, How India Became Democratic

contribution: Pedagogical state, codification, representation and the conceptual architecture of the founding.
limitations: High-level reconstruction; contested by other readings of mass democracy and social power.
source_label: [S20] Madhav Khosla, India’s Founding Moment

contribution: How citizens, litigants and groups activated the Constitution; law as social and political practice.
limitations: Primarily early republican afterlife; use as outgoing preservation/reception layer.
source_label: [S21] Rohit De, A People’s Constitution

contribution: B. N. Rau, adviser–committee relations and the normative politics of drafting; controls sole-author myth.
limitations: Centres Rau; must still preserve Drafting Committee and Assembly agency.
source_label: [S22] Arvind Elangovan, Norms and Politics

contribution: Protective discrimination, caste, reservations and equality jurisprudence.
limitations: Later legal-institutional focus; distinguish 1950 settlement from subsequent policy/law.
source_label: [S23] Marc Galanter, Competing Equalities

contribution: Focused reassessment of Poona Pact, representation and electoral consequences.
limitations: One intervention in a contested field; triangulate with pact, award, election data and Ambedkar’s later statements.
source_label: [S24] Simanti Biswas, “Did the Poona Pact Disenfranchise the Depressed Classes?”
